necessary_context.content: Section 2 uses Stief(d,r)={V in R^(d by r): V^T V=I}, descending eigenvalues lambda_i(M), singular values sigma_i(M), and abs(M)=(M^2)^(1/2). Definition 2.1 permits randomized adaptive exact vector queries v^(i), responses M v^(i), and output Vhat in Stief(d,r). Each vector query counts individually; there is no Krylov or output-span restriction in that definition.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p4, Section 2 notation, Definition 2.1 and Example 2.1
necessary_context.name: Query model and matrix notation

necessary_context.content: Definition 2.2: upper-triangular entries are independent, W_ij~N(0,1/d) for i<j and W_ii~N(0,2/d); W is symmetric. For Theorem 2.2, M=W+lambda U U^T with U uniform on Stief(d,r), independent of W; g in (0,1), lambda=(1+sqrt(g(2-g)))/(1-g). Equation (2.1): g=(lambda-1)^2/(lambda^2+1).
necessary_context.locator: PDF pp4–5, Definition 2.2, Proposition 2.1, Equation (2.1), Theorem 2.2
necessary_context.name: GOE and planted matrix

necessary_context.content: E_good(gamma)={||W||op+(1-gamma)(lambda+lambda^(-1)-2)<=lambda_r(M)} intersect {lambda_1(M)<=(1+gamma)(lambda+lambda^(-1))}. Proposition 2.1 states its probability guarantee only for gamma,delta in (0,1/10). Theorem 2.2 instead invokes q(g^(-1),(1-g)^(-1),2,r,log(2)) and conditions on E_good(1/2). These are distinct parameter scopes; their transfer is not established here.
